title: Opening the Cafe
steps: Unlock the back door by 6:00 AM and enter your personal code on the alarm keypad within 30 seconds.
Turn on the lights at the panel by the back door.
Switch on the espresso machine and let it heat for at least 30 minutes before the first shot.
If the machine won't turn on, check that the breaker labeled "Espresso" in the office electrical panel is on and that the water valve under the bar counter is open.
Turn on both grinders and the batch brewer.
Count the opening till to ensure it holds $150 ($100 in small bills and $50 in coins).
Record the count on the till sheet and notify the manager if the amount is off by more than $2.

The till sheet is on the clipboard hanging inside the office door, next to the safe. Start a new sheet each morning, and file the finished sheet from the day before in the red binder on the office shelf.
The manager on duty is listed on the weekly schedule posted in the office. If no manager is in yet, text the owner using the number on the contact list by the office phone.
Dial in the espresso by pulling a test shot with 18 grams of coffee to yield 36 grams in 25 to 30 seconds; adjust grind size based on shot time.
Brew the first batch of house drip coffee and record the brew time on the airpot label.
The bakery leaves the pastry delivery in the covered plastic bins inside the back door around 5:30 AM. Bring the bins to the bar first thing.
Stock the pastry case from the morning delivery and place a price tag in front of each item.
The price tags are in the top drawer under the pastry case, sorted by item.
Fill the milk fridge under the bar with whole, 2%, oat, and almond milk.

Any time milk is poured out (expired, spilled, or used in a remade drink), write the item, amount, and reason on the waste sheet on the clipboard behind the bar. The manager reviews the waste sheet each week to set the milk order.
Unlock the front door and flip the sign to Open at 6:30 AM.
warnings: Never open the front door before the till is counted.
Pour out drip coffee that has been sitting for more than 30 minutes.
If the alarm goes off, call the alarm company right away and give them the passcode on the card in the office.

If the espresso machine still isn't ready after 45 minutes, call the repair service number on the sticker on the side of the machine and tell the manager on duty. Until it's fixed, serve only drip coffee, cold brew, and tea, and put the "Espresso Unavailable" sign on the counter.

title: Closing the Cafe
steps: Stop brewing new batch coffee at 5:45 PM.
At 6:00 PM, lock the front door, flip the sign to Closed, and pour out any remaining drip coffee.
Clean the espresso machine following the Espresso Machine Daily Cleaning procedure.
The 'Espresso Machine Daily Cleaning' procedure document is in Handoff. Open Procedures and select Espresso Machine Daily Cleaning, or ask Handoff a question about cleaning the machine.
Count the till with a second employee present and leave exactly $150 in the drawer for the next morning.

If the till count does not match the register report, count it a second time with the other closing employee. If it is still off by more than $2, write the difference on the till sheet, seal the deposit as usual, and text the manager on duty, who is listed on the weekly schedule in the office.
Put the remaining cash and the day's register report in a deposit bag, seal it, and drop it in the office safe.
Log unsold pastries on the waste sheet and throw them out; nothing in the case carries over to the next day.
The waste sheet is on the clipboard behind the bar.
Wipe down the counters, sweep and mop the floor, and take out the trash and recycling.
Check that the milk fridge reads 41°F or below and write the temperature on the log.
The temperature log is taped to the door of the milk fridge under the bar.

If the milk fridge temperature is above 41°F, make sure the fridge door is fully closed and nothing is blocking the vent, then check again after 30 minutes. If it is still above 41°F, move all the milk to the walk-in overnight, write the problem on the temperature log, and tell the manager on duty.
Turn off the grinders, batch brewer, and lights, set the alarm, and lock the back door.

If the alarm won't set, check that every door and the office window are fully closed, then try again. If it still won't set, call the alarm company using the number on the card in the office and tell the manager on duty. If the back door won't lock, never leave the building unlocked. Call the manager and wait inside with the other closing employee until the manager or a locksmith arrives.
warnings: Never leave more than the $150 starting bank in the register overnight.
Leave the espresso machine on overnight; it is designed to stay on, and restarting it every day wears out the heating element.
Never take cash from the deposit or your own pocket to cover a difference.
Throw out any milk that was above 41°F for more than 4 hours.

title: Espresso Machine Daily Cleaning
steps: Remove each portafilter and knock out the used coffee puck after the final shot.
Insert the blind basket into a portafilter and add half a teaspoon of espresso machine detergent.
Use Cafiza espresso machine cleaning powder, the blue tub in the chemical cabinet.
Lock the portafilter into the group head and run the backflush cycle (10 seconds on, 10 seconds off) five times.
Rinse the blind basket and repeat the backflush cycle five times with plain water.
Soak portafilter baskets and spouts in a solution of one tablespoon of detergent per liter of hot water for 20 minutes, then rinse and dry.
Soak the portafilter baskets and spouts in the gray soaking bin in the back sink.
Scrub group head gaskets and shower screens using the group head brush.
Purge each steam wand for three seconds, wipe with the steam wand cloth, and soak steam tips in hot water for 10 minutes.
Soak the steam tips separately in a cup of plain hot water next to the gray soaking bin, not in the detergent.
Empty and rinse the drip tray, then wipe down the machine exterior.
Pull one water-only shot through each group head to flush residual detergent.
Leave the machine on overnight.
Hang the group head brush and the steam wand cloths on the hooks to the right of the espresso machine.
Put used cloths in the laundry bin in the back room and hang a clean cloth for the morning.
warnings: Never submerge portafilter handles as soaking damages them.
Backflush with detergent only once daily to prevent gasket wear.
If a group head leaks during backflushing, stop immediately and notify the manager for potential gasket replacement.
Espresso machine detergent is stored in the chemical cabinet under the back sink, on the bottom shelf, away from food and milk.
Never substitute dish soap, because it foams and leaves residue inside the machine.

title: Receiving Deliveries and Cold Storage
steps: Check each delivery against the invoice before signing and write any missing or damaged items on the invoice.
Ask the driver to initial the change on the invoice, then text a photo of the invoice to the manager on duty, who is listed on the weekly schedule in the office.
Check milk and dairy with the probe thermometer and reject anything above 41°F.
Keep the probe thermometer in its case, and wipe the tip with an alcohol wipe before and after each use.
Put cold items away first, within 15 minutes of the delivery arriving.
Label every item with the date received using the day-dot stickers.
The day-dot stickers and probe thermometers are located in the drawer next to the walk-in door.
Rotate stock first in, first out: move older items to the front and place the new delivery behind them.
In the walk-in, store raw ingredients on the lower shelves and ready-to-eat items above them.
Keep alternative milks and nut-based syrups on their own labeled shelf, separate from dairy.
Break down the boxes for recycling and leave the signed invoice in the manager's tray.
warnings: Do not accept a delivery if the driver will not wait for you to check it.

Hand rejected items straight back to the driver before they leave; do not put them away. If the driver has already left, put the items on the shelf marked "Do Not Use" in the walk-in and tell the manager on duty.
Throw out any dairy past its use-by date, even if it smells fine.
Keep the walk-in door closed; it must stay at 41°F or below.

If the walk-in temperature is above 41°F, make sure the door closes fully and the fan inside is running, then check again after 30 minutes. If it is still above 41°F, move the milk and dairy to the milk fridge under the bar, write the temperature on the temperature log, and tell the manager on duty, who will call the refrigeration repair company.
Throw out anything that was above 41°F for more than 4 hours.

title: Allergen and Alternative Milk Orders
steps: Repeat the allergy back to the customer.
Press the 'Allergy' button on the register order.

Press the Allergy button on each item that is for the customer with the allergy, not on the whole order. The ticket then marks only those items, so the barista knows exactly which drinks need the allergen steps.
Verbally alert the barista to the specific allergy and drink item.
Use a clean pitcher from the green allergen shelf for alternative milks.
The green allergen shelf is located on the left end of the bar, directly above the milk fridge. It has a green label and holds only the allergen pitchers and sealed syrup bottles.
Purge the steam wand for three seconds and wipe with a fresh cloth.
Use only sealed syrup bottles, being aware that almond and hazelnut syrups contain tree nuts.
After each use, wash the allergen pitcher in the back sink with hot, soapy water, rinse it, and let it air-dry on the green allergen shelf.
Personally hand the drink to the customer and confirm the allergy by name.
If uncertain about safety, present the ingredient binder at the register to the customer.

The ingredient binder is stored on the shelf under the register, labeled "Ingredients." Every drink and pastry has its own page listing its allergens, and the manager updates the binder whenever the menu changes.
warnings: Never promise that an item is allergen-free; our kitchen handles common allergens.
Our pastries come from a bakery that handles wheat, eggs, milk, and tree nuts.
If a customer has an allergic reaction, call 911 first, then the manager.
Call 911 first, and never wait for a manager before calling. Then contact the manager on duty, who is listed on the weekly schedule in the office.
Never put allergen pitchers in the dish bin with the regular pitchers.

title: Customer Complaints and Remakes
steps: Listen to the whole complaint without interrupting, then apologize.
Offer to remake any drink the customer is unhappy with, free of charge.
If the customer does not want a remake, offer a refund following the Register Refunds and Voids procedure.
The 'Register Refunds and Voids procedure' documentation is in Handoff. Open Procedures and select Register Refunds and Voids, or ask Handoff how to give a refund.
Log every remake on the waste sheet with the reason, such as 'too sweet' or 'wrong milk.'
The waste sheet is a paper sheet on the clipboard behind the bar.
If the same customer complains a second time during the same visit, get the manager.
If the complaint is about an employee, thank the customer, write down the details, and give them to the manager that day.

If the manager is not on-site, seal the written details in an envelope marked "For the Manager" and leave it in the manager's tray in the office. Then text the manager on duty that a complaint note is waiting.
Give a free drink card to any customer whose order was wrong because of our mistake.
Free drink cards are kept in an envelope in the register drawer, under the cash tray. Write the date and your initials on the back of every card you give out.
warnings: Never argue with a customer about whether a drink was made correctly.
Remakes are always free, but refunds over $20 need manager approval.
Do not discuss the complaint with the employee it is about.

title: Register Refunds and Voids
steps: To void an item, select the item on the order screen and press Void before the customer pays.
To issue a refund, locate the original sale in Order History using the receipt number or the last four digits of the card.
If a customer loses their receipt and does not know the last four digits of their card, search Order History by the date, the approximate time, and the total amount.
If you still can't find the sale, you can't refund it. Offer a free remake or a free drink card instead, and let the manager on duty know.
Drinks and food can only be refunded on the same day they were bought. Unopened bags of coffee beans and merchandise can be refunded within 14 days with a receipt or a match in Order History.
For card sales, process the refund back to the original card.
For cash sales, process the refund from the drawer.
For refunds over $20, obtain a manager's approval code.
Record every cash refund on the till sheet, including the amount and reason.

The till sheet stays on the clipboard inside the office door, next to the safe. Write the refund on it as soon as the customer leaves. It stays on the clipboard until closing, and the next morning's opener files it in the red binder on the office shelf.
Print the refund receipt and provide it to the customer.
warnings: Never refund a card payment in cash.
Never void an item after the customer has paid; issue a refund instead.
Card refunds take 3 to 5 business days to appear on the customer's statement.
No approval is needed for voids.

If the system fails or prevents a refund from processing, do not give cash to get around a card refund. Write the customer's name, phone number, the amount, and the date and time of the original sale on the till sheet. Tell the customer the manager will finish the refund within one business day, and text the manager on duty.
